# The Interstellar Song Contest

**The Interstellar Song Contest** is the sixth episode of the second series (15th overall series) of the British science fiction television series *Doctor Who*, first broadcast on BBC One and Disney+ on 17 May 2025 . The episode was written by Juno Dawson and directed by Ben A. Williams . It features Ncuti Gatwa as the Fifteenth Doctor and Varada Sethu as his companion Belinda Chandra .

The episode draws direct inspiration from the Eurovision Song Contest, with the 69th edition of Eurovision being broadcast on the same day as the episode's premiere . Real-life Eurovision commentators Rylan Clark and Graham Norton appear in the episode playing themselves . The episode has been noted as the most expensive to produce in the entire history of *Doctor Who* .

## Production

### Development

The concept for "The Interstellar Song Contest" originated with showrunner Russell T. Davies, who pitched the basic premise as "Die Hard meets Eurovision" to writer Juno Dawson in 2022 . Dawson later recalled that Davies emailed her at approximately 1:30 in the morning with this concept . The writer, who had previously worked on the *Doctor Who* spinoff podcast *Doctor Who Redacted*, described it as "the easiest 'yes' I've ever said" .

Dawson initially proposed a more ambitious concept inspired by the disaster film *The Poseidon Adventure*, but this was deemed prohibitively expensive to produce . She later expressed mild embarrassment about this initial idea, stating, "I look back now with a slight cringe" . The final script maintained the core concept of "Eurovision meets Die Hard" throughout the development process .

### Crew and Cast

The episode was written by Juno Dawson, making it the first episode in *Doctor Who* history to be written by an openly transgender person . The episode was directed by Ben A. Williams , with Vicki Delow serving as producer . Executive producers included Russell T. Davies, Julie Gardner, Jane Tranter, and Joel Collins .

The cast featured Ncuti Gatwa as the Fifteenth Doctor and Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra . The episode marked the return of several classic *Doctor Who* characters, including Carole Ann Ford reprising her role as Susan Foreman, the Doctor's granddaughter, who had not appeared in the series since 1964 . Anita Dobson played Mrs. Flood, while Archie Panjabi was introduced as The Rani .

The guest cast included Freddie Fox as the villainous Kid, Kadiff Kirwan as Mike Gabbastone, Charlie Condou as Gary Gabbastone, and Miriam-Teak Lee as Cora St Bavier . Rylan Clark and Graham Norton appeared as themselves, reprising their roles as Eurovision commentators .

### Production Costs

"The Interstellar Song Contest" has been confirmed as the most expensive episode in the entire history of *Doctor Who* . Despite this significant budget, some viewers and critics noted that the episode only "fleetingly looked the part" compared to other high-budget science fiction productions like *Andor*, which has a reported budget of nearly \$300 million per season .

The high production costs are evident in several elaborate sequences, including the scene where 100,000 spectators are blown into space, which required extensive special effects work . The episode also features complex holographic effects and detailed alien creature designs .

## Plot Summary

The episode begins with the Doctor and Belinda arriving at the Harmony Arena space station in the year 2925, just in time for the 803rd Interstellar Song Contest . They witness Rylan Clark emerging from cryogenic suspension to host the event . The Doctor and Belinda decide to watch the contest from VIP boxes, intrigued by the spectacle .

As the contest begins, trouble quietly brews in the background. Mrs. Flood, sitting in the audience, secretly copies the Doctor's vindicator reading onto her own device, describing it as "the final link" she needs . Meanwhile, in the control gallery, the production team's security drone guards are hijacked by an interloping Hellion known as "Kid" .

Kid and his accomplice Wynn, another Hellion who had infiltrated the production team, take control of the Harmony Arena and the contest's broadcast . They switch the broadcast to a dress rehearsal and open the air shield of the arena, causing the entire audience, including the Doctor and the TARDIS, to be sucked into space .

Frozen in space and barely conscious, the Doctor has a vision of his granddaughter Susan Foreman, who tells him to go back and find her . He wakes from his stasis and uses a nearby confetti cannon to propel himself back to the Harmony Arena, where he is resuscitated by paramedic Mike Gabbastone, who is attending the event with his husband Gary .

While the Doctor, Mike, and Gary search for answers, Belinda encounters other survivors in the arena, including contest favorite Cora St Bavier, who was representing the planet Trion . When the survivors discover that Hellions are behind the attack, Cora reveals herself to be a Hellion in hiding. She explains that Kid and Wynn are seeking vengeance against the contest's sponsor, a corporation that razed their home planet of Hellia for its natural resource, the Hell Poppy, and then blamed the atrocity on the native population .

Enraged by this injustice and the apparent death of Belinda (whom he believes was also sucked into space), the Doctor seeks out the Hellions and destroys their delta wave device, which they had planned to use to kill the three trillion viewers of the contest . Using a hard-light hologram, the Doctor repeatedly electrocutes Kid, ignoring Susan's pleas in his mind to stop .

The Doctor eventually stops his attack and works to save the frozen audience members using the station's "mavity" field, which has suspended them in a state of preservation . Cora is given the opportunity to sing a song in honor of her destroyed home planet Hellia for the three trillion viewers .

As the Doctor and Belinda prepare to leave, they encounter a hologram of Graham Norton, who reveals that Earth was destroyed on May 24, 2025 . The Doctor immediately departs to try to save Earth on that date.

In a mid-credits scene, Mrs. Flood is revealed to be The Rani, who has bi-generated into two separate beings: herself and the elderly Mrs. Flood . The Rani declares her intention to seek revenge against the Doctor .

## Reception

### Critical Response

"The Interstellar Song Contest" received mixed reviews from critics. Radio Times gave the episode a perfect 5 out of 5 stars, describing it as "a magnificent spin on Eurovision sprinkled with the stuff of legends" . Patrick Mulkern praised the episode's blend of camp Eurovision-style entertainment with high-stakes science fiction adventure .

Out Front Magazine gave the episode a 96/100 rating, calling it "one of the best and most exciting episodes of the entire series" . The review particularly praised the episode for being written by a transgender woman and noted its themes of colonization and genocide as subtle commentary on contemporary issues .

However, other critics were more critical. Doctor Who TV's review was highly critical, stating that the episode "sabotages itself" through inconsistent storytelling . The review specifically criticized the episode's handling of the frozen audience, noting that the script "can't decide if the audience is dead or not, turning them into Schrödinger's spectators" . The review also faulted the episode's "not-so-science fiction" elements, particularly the technobabble explanation involving the "mavity" field .

Den of Geek's review described the episode as "a land of contrasts" and noted that it "can't settle on a consistent tone" . The review praised the episode's visual spectacle and the performances of Rylan Clark and Graham Norton but criticized the Doctor's sudden shift to violent behavior as unearned and out of character .

Film Stories offered a more balanced review, noting that "the song contest stuff is really well realised" and praising the episode's glossy production values . However, the review also noted that the episode struggled to develop the dynamic between the Doctor and Belinda .

### Audience Reaction

Social media reaction to the episode was largely positive, with many fans praising the return of Carole Ann Ford as Susan Foreman . Several prominent *Doctor Who* fans and writers, including Simon Guerrier, David, Paul Cornell, John F.P. Lane, and Tom Newsom, publicly praised the episode and writer Juno Dawson .

The episode's timing, airing on the same night as the actual Eurovision Song Contest, was widely noted and appreciated by fans . Many viewers enjoyed the meta-humor of having real Eurovision commentators appearing in the episode .

## Cultural Impact

### Eurovision Connection

"The Interstellar Song Contest" was deliberately scheduled to air on the same day as the 69th Eurovision Song Contest, creating a unique viewing experience for British audiences . The episode's premise is essentially a science fiction version of Eurovision, extrapolated into the year 2925 as the 803rd edition of an intergalactic competition .

The episode features several elements that directly reference Eurovision, including the format of the contest, the voting system, and the presence of Rylan Clark and Graham Norton as commentators . The character of Rylan Clark is portrayed as having been cryogenically preserved and unfrozen annually to host the Interstellar Song Contest , which fans found particularly amusing.

### Social Commentary

The episode incorporates several themes of social and political commentary. The character of Cora St Bavier, a Hellion who has cut off her horns to fit in with mainstream society, serves as a metaphor for the extremes some people go to in order to conform . This has been interpreted by some viewers as a commentary on transgender identity and the pressures of societal acceptance .

The episode also addresses themes of racial stereotyping and xenophobia through the portrayal of Hellions. In one scene, Cora overhears her manager Len accusing Hellions of practicing cannibalism and witchcraft . This sequence is particularly poignant as both characters are portrayed by Black actors, visually emphasizing that they share more in common than just business interests .

The character of Kid represents a more complex take on villainy, as his actions are driven by legitimate grievances. His home planet Hellia was destroyed by corporate greed, stripped of its natural resources for artificial honey flavoring . This storyline has been interpreted as commentary on colonialism, corporate exploitation, and environmental destruction .

### Historical Significance

"The Interstellar Song Contest" holds several significant milestones in *Doctor Who* history. It marks the first time the series has been written by an openly transgender person , a fact that was widely celebrated by both fans and the media.

The episode also features the long-awaited return of Carole Ann Ford as Susan Foreman, the Doctor's granddaughter, who had not appeared in the series since 1964 . Ford's appearance, while brief, was highly anticipated by long-time fans and has sparked speculation about her potential role in future episodes .

The episode also introduces the character of The Rani in a new incarnation, played by Archie Panjabi . The character's return, combined with the revelation that she has bi-generated into two separate beings, has created significant buzz among fans about the direction of the series .

## Legacy

"The Interstellar Song Contest" has already begun to establish its legacy within the *Doctor Who* franchise. The episode's high production values and ambitious scope have set a new standard for the series, particularly in terms of visual effects and set design .

The episode's themes and story elements are likely to have long-lasting implications for the series. The return of The Rani and the appearance of Susan Foreman have both been positioned as major plot points that will likely be revisited in future episodes .

The episode's success has also helped to establish Juno Dawson as an important new voice in *Doctor Who* writing. Her ability to balance camp entertainment with social commentary and character development has been widely praised .

The Interstellar Song Contest itself has become a notable fictional event within the *Doctor Who* universe. As a futuristic version of Eurovision that has expanded to include planets across the galaxy , it represents the kind of optimistic, interconnected future that the series often portrays.

Juno Dawson and Freddie Fox (Images: Attitude/BBC)

**[Juno Dawson](https://www.attitude.co.uk/tag/juno-dawson/)** has teased further details of the Eurovision-inspired **[episode of _Doctor Who_ she penned.](https://www.attitude.co.uk/culture/doctor-whojuno-dawson-says-episode-shes-writing-is-most-expensive-ever-exclusive-479745/)**

The episode, which centres around an enemy faction planning an attack on the ‘Interstellar Song Contest’, is due to air on Saturday ahead of the actual Eurovision Song Contest on which it was based.

#### Read next

*   [##### ‘I think Abe Lincoln might be a leather daddy’: Mason Alexander Park on bringing cult comedy Oh Mary! to the West End (EXCLUSIVE)](https://www.attitude.co.uk/culture/mason-alexander-park-oh-mary-west-end-interview-507261/)
*   [##### Show me the receipts: Examining Pope Leo XIV’s history of LGBTQ-related statements and actions](https://www.attitude.co.uk/news/world/show-me-the-receipts-pope-leo-xiv-507249/)

Dawson revealed that showrunner **[Russell T Davies](https://www.attitude.co.uk/tag/russell-t-davies)** came to her with a basic premise from which she expanded. “Russell initially pitched the bare bones concept of Eurovision meets _Die Hard_, which were two things I knew really well,” she recalled.

“Then, I went away and pitched a plot, and it hasn’t really changed all that much. Obviously, there was a lot of discussion between myself, the producers and Russell. But it’s still those two things. What would happen if an enemy faction planned an attack on the Eurovision Song Contest in space?”

The episode includes guest appearances from Rylan Clark, who plays the host of the song contest, and **[Freddie Fox, who plays Kid](https://www.attitude.co.uk/culture/film-tv/doc-480802/)**, a villain leading the enemy attack. When asked to describe the episode with just one phrase, Dawson remarked: “Freddie Fox looks good with horns.”

She went on to say: “It’s like a disaster movie. I think people are certainly going to expect it to be … let’s just say camp. I mean of course it is, it’s the Interstellar Song Contest. But also, it’s action-packed. It doesn’t let up for a second. It’s a really high-octane episode.”

Fox, who has previously worked with Davies on the 2015 Channel 4 queer drama _Cucumber_, echoed Dawson’s sentiments, revealing: “Audiences can expect to see the most audacious interpretation of Eurovision ever conceived, bigger than even Eurovision itself.

“I thought this is camp, camp, camp!” Fox explained. “Russell, how do you even think of it, let alone make it so brilliant? I think it’s going to blow the audiences minds.”

The actor had high praise for Dawson also. “I worked quite hard on making Kid as specific as I could. He was such a well written character by Juno, who wrote the script.”

_Doctor Who_ is available to watch on BBC iPlayer from 8am on Saturday morning and on BBC One at 7.10pm that evening.

9.description: Doctor Who visited the Interstellar Song Contest last night, for an episode that generated a lot of fan comments on THOSE reveals!
9.content:
[![Image 1: The Doctor (NCUTI GATWA) & Belinda Chandra (VARADA SETHU) cheer on the contestants at The Interstellar Song Contest COPYRIGHT:BBC Studios/Bad Wolf,CREDIT LINE:BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon. The two hold their hands in the air cheering, sitting in a round, futuristic, viewing platform.](https://www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/519388-scaled.jpg)](https://i0.wp.com/www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/519388-scaled.jpg?fit=2560%2C1707&quality=89&ssl=1)

The Doctor (NCUTI GATWA) & Belinda Chandra (VARADA SETHU) cheer on the contestants at The Interstellar Song Contest COPYRIGHT:BBC Studios/Bad Wolf,CREDIT LINE:BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Doctor Who** heads to _The Interstellar Song Contest_ for a night of song, danger, and surprises that left fans smiling
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

First things first. Football. There was a very real danger of the FA Cup final overrunning which would have meant **Doctor Who** being exiled to **BBC Two** for the week. Or even worse. Neil Norman expressed the relief of all the fans tuning it at 7.05 to discover that the, eh, sporters in stripey tops beat the non-stripey ones to lift the trophy just in time.

> “I felt a great disturbance in the Force, as if millions of Doctor Who fans suddenly breathed a huge sigh of relief.”
> 
> 
> — [Neil Norman And His Cosmic Orchestra (@fubsyshabaroon.bsky.social)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:rmtwa32ujm464l3mm45wjoob?ref_src=embed)[2025-05-17T17:47:57.793Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:rmtwa32ujm464l3mm45wjoob/post/3lpf3zwuhcc25?ref_src=embed)

The response to _The Interstellar Song Contest_ was even more positive this week, in a season that’s been widely loved online. Simon Guerrier, David, Paul Cornell, John FP Lane, and Tom Newsom were just some of those heaping praise on the episode as well as writer Juno Dawson.

> LOVED THAT #DoctorWho
> 
> 
> — [Simon Guerrier (@0tralala.bsky.social)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:lqgtdd3dx7fzfa2nyndygqjd?ref_src=embed)[2025-05-17T18:58:04.570Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:lqgtdd3dx7fzfa2nyndygqjd/post/3lpf7xcqigk26?ref_src=embed)

> Well that was a great #DoctorWho. In taking on a big real world event it reminded me of Fear Her but worked much better. It made perfect sense of Mrs Flood, which I was beginning to doubt could be done. A nuanced treatment of oppression and resistance. Also MAVITY! And two women from the past…
> 
> 
> — [David (@bluebookballoon.bsky.social)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:t7orbdscclvcng2sevwldyee?ref_src=embed)[2025-05-17T19:43:49.708Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:t7orbdscclvcng2sevwldyee/post/3lpfcj4pgbs2i?ref_src=embed)

> Great stuff @junodawson.bsky.social ! Excellently paced, huge world building, enormous heart! Full marks from the Gloucestershire jury! #DoctorWho
> 
> 
> — [Paul Cornell (@paulcornell.bsky.social)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:bu3qvbmhtfhz2zgbnxym34lm?ref_src=embed)[2025-05-17T07:48:25.970Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:bu3qvbmhtfhz2zgbnxym34lm/post/3lpe2jvgxds2m?ref_src=embed)

> Phenomenal Doctor Who this week! Hope everyone enjoyed it too. (How they packed all that into 50 mins I don't know!)
> 
> 
> — [Tom Newsom (@aquatics64.bsky.social)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:4jxcnnlnvq6e3jctn2tcxnm4?ref_src=embed)[2025-05-17T10:32:12.445Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:4jxcnnlnvq6e3jctn2tcxnm4/post/3lpedoqs6zc2y?ref_src=embed)

> Honestly, I lapped that right up! #DoctorWho
> 
> 
> — [John FP Lane (@jfplane.bsky.social)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:k5rtna73nnjy52t6yijlu6gj?ref_src=embed)[2025-05-17T20:23:15.138Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:k5rtna73nnjy52t6yijlu6gj/post/3lpfepmkses2v?ref_src=embed)

Richard the Sod is not the first person this year to reckon Ncuti Gatwa’s second season is the best in 20 years.**Blogtor** has a lot of time too for Huw Bowen pointing out that **Doctor Who** as a show is preposterous, unhinged… and very good indeed.

> This has easily been the best season of Doctor Who since the show came back. What an episode.
> 
> 
> — [Richard The Sod (@richardthesod.bsky.social)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:wq3z622af6hjeaqvuomz2aqc?ref_src=embed)[2025-05-17T20:22:50.110Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:wq3z622af6hjeaqvuomz2aqc/post/3lpfeouov2s2c?ref_src=embed)

> Doctor Who continues to be one of the most preposterous shows on tv and I am still loving it. Tonight's episode was extremely unhinged and very good indeed
> 
> 
> — [Huw Bowen / Sundog (@huwbowen.bsky.social)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:mow5pm2szwqmu37wzqibivzu?ref_src=embed)[2025-05-17T20:12:22.398Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:mow5pm2szwqmu37wzqibivzu/post/3lpfe462m3k2z?ref_src=embed)

Another observation that’s been made by many this season, is how much like late 1980s **Doctor Who** it feels. Richard Unwin and Paul Burley are just the latest to chime in, commenting that _The Interstellar Song Contest_ is the type of thing legendary showunner JNT would have done. If only he could have afforded it.

> Doctor Who just made my brain fall out. Camp and joyful – like a modern Season 24 – with a glorious secret at its heart! And one of my favourite Ncuti performances ever. #DoctorWho
> 
> 
> — [Richard Unwin (@richardunwin.bsky.social)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:2ke67oyjkdzimhtipxrucyz7?ref_src=embed)[2025-05-17T12:20:15.709Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:2ke67oyjkdzimhtipxrucyz7/post/3lpejpxmmv22d?ref_src=embed)

> It's very "if John Nathan-Turner had the budget", isn't it? (And I don't mean that in a pissy way.) #DoctorWho
> 
> 
> — [Paul Burley (@paulburley.bsky.social)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:pgv43ow7j6coy633aysyhs27?ref_src=embed)[2025-05-17T18:31:43.066Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:pgv43ow7j6coy633aysyhs27/post/3lpf6i6irxc2p?ref_src=embed)

### There was also huge pleasure at the two shock reveals of returning characters this week

As epic and fun as th**e Eurovision** in Space aspect was, for a lot of people it was all about the two big shock reveals. As Lisa Grimm says…

> No spoilers, but you get to punch the air TWICE, fellow Who nerds. Just saying.
> 
> 
> — [Lisa Grimm (@lisagrimm.com)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:bjovrbtmnlckoh6vaalnqjzi?ref_src=embed)[2025-05-17T07:50:47.214Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:bjovrbtmnlckoh6vaalnqjzi/post/3lpe2o45cyc2s?ref_src=embed)

The cameos by Carole Ann Ford as Susan, the Doctor’s granddaughter, telepathically warning him, first to keep on trying, and secondly to stop his brutal attack, begins to fulfills an age old promise to one day come back to her. It’s something fans have wanted to see for decades, as Vinyl Constituency suggests with his one word comment: _“Finally.”_

> Finally. ♥️👇🏻#DoctorWho #Susan
> 
> 
> — [The Vinyl Constituency (@vinylconstituency.bsky.social)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:lfan3znioe5ujzlxhvexx6s7?ref_src=embed)[2025-05-17T20:01:50.832Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:lfan3znioe5ujzlxhvexx6s7/post/3lpfdjdr26k2a?ref_src=embed)

> Blimey! I was not expecting that! #DoctorWho
> 
> 
> — [Paul Hayes (@paul-hayes.bsky.social)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:i7xcdhrmunjskrznowqwdljs?ref_src=embed)[2025-05-17T08:53:11.922Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:i7xcdhrmunjskrznowqwdljs/post/3lpe65peqfc2u?ref_src=embed)

The other returning Time Lord of 20th century **Doctor Who** has a new face. Or, rather, two new faces. Archie Panjabi is the new Rani (the definite article you might say.) There’s only one world to describe her, and Steve finds it:

> Queen!
> 
> 
> — [Steve 🏳️‍🌈🇬🇧 (@wohyeahwohyeah.bsky.social)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:dfrlhxcvlscyo6l4xxcedzvl?ref_src=embed)[2025-05-17T19:33:48.784Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:dfrlhxcvlscyo6l4xxcedzvl/post/3lpfbx7n62s2q?ref_src=embed)

“Who? _Who?_**WHO?!**” Stef realizes not everybody already knows the Rani, but it shouldn’t ruin the fun.

> RTD2 era of Doctor Who is summed up by classic villains returning and Nu-Who fans going ‘who?!’ in the best way possible
> 
> 
> — [Stef. (@stefham97.bsky.social)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:leaj5dodni2pufiitbu2k6x5?ref_src=embed)[2025-05-17T19:49:40.079Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:leaj5dodni2pufiitbu2k6x5/post/3lpfctktvhk27?ref_src=embed)

Of course, Archie Panjabi may be _the_ Rani, but Anita Dobson’s Mrs. Flood is _a_ Rani. Wicca Fenian is just one of many, many, fans, celebrating getting their guess right. But then fans have been guessing every other female character is the Rani since 2005. They had to be right some time.

> Totally called it on the identity of Mrs Flood on Doctor Who. By that, I mean I had 86 theories and that was definitely one of them 😂
> 
> 
> — [(@wiccafenian.bsky.social)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:p7gc52753dbyzo4w5e26gv2k?ref_src=embed)[2025-05-17T20:04:11.861Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:p7gc52753dbyzo4w5e26gv2k/post/3lpfdnkam2c2q?ref_src=embed)

Paul Lang suspects that memories of Kate O’Mara’s fantastically arch 1980s incarnation of the Rani means the character’s return played out to identical scenes on screen and at home.

> Feels SO right that the Rani’s rebirth should be witnessed by two slack-jawed 50-year-old gays. Absolutely loved every second of that. #DoctorWho
> 
> 
> — [Paul (@rudemrlang.bsky.social)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:zpj6i4sszug2ehlc5p7tyym3?ref_src=embed)[2025-05-17T18:58:33.697Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:zpj6i4sszug2ehlc5p7tyym3/post/3lpf7y6jerc2w?ref_src=embed)

Final word goes to Andrew Orton, who remembers what happened last time the Rani and Mel were in an episode together. Suddenly**Blogtor** wants absolutely nothing else from _Wish World_ than this.

> She’d better dress up as Bonnie Langford next week #DoctorWhoSpoilers #spoilers
> 
> 
> — [Andrew Orton (@andreworton.bsky.social)](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:h2tgvjw6vgyhxsiw6he55yc3?ref_src=embed)[2025-05-17T19:59:08.238Z](https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:h2tgvjw6vgyhxsiw6he55yc3/post/3lpfdeior7k2u?ref_src=embed)

[](https://i0.wp.com/www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/090524-JPP-WHO-00630-scaled.jpg?quality=89)

Conrad (Jonah Hauer-King) The Rani (Archie Panjabi) Mrs Flood/aka The Rani (Anita Dobson): Wish World’s Unholy Trinity BBC Studios/Bad Wolf

### **Doctor Who** continues with _Wish World_ at 6.50pm this Saturday on **BBC One**. Episodes also drop on [**iPlayer**](https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m002cswr) in the UK and **Disney+** everywhere else (except Ireland) at 8am GMT.

12.title: TV Review: The 'Doctor Who' Episode 'The Interstellar Song Contest' Serves Up Major Surprises and a Pop-Culture Tribute
12.description: This episode offers surprise appearances from classic 'Doctor Who' in one of the show’s most exciting pop-culture tributes.
12.content:
[![Image 1: CCC LB 2025](https://cdn.broadstreetads.com/assets/7a297666-601b-4dc1-b1b3-6eff11d6ab93.jpg)](https://denverconvention.com/ "CCC LB 2025")

Another thing I love about _Doctor Who_ is the twists and turns, the surprise comebacks, and the exciting sudden reversals. In other words, _Doctor Who_ is cheap melodrama, and I love a good, cheap, melodrama. In the latest episode, “The Interstellar Song Contest,” the show offers up a lot of surprises in a quick amount of time, in addition to offering up a tribute to the popular _Eurovision Song Contest_ even as the actual contest is taking place, as well as giving us the first episode in the history of _Doctor Who_ to be written by an openly transgender person, namely the famous trans children’s author Juno Dawson, perhaps most famous for her book _This Book is Gay_. All of that combined to make one of the biggest and best episodes of an already great series, and one that will possibly be remembered as one of the last greats.

Since the episode is so deeply inspired by [_Eurovision_](https://outfrontmagazine.com/netta-is-a-mother-fcking-ceo/), it might make sense to explain to Americans a little bit about what _Eurovision_ is. The _Eurovision Song Contest_ is an annual songwriting and singing competition organized by the European Broadcasting Union. Each European nation in the contest sends one original song and performer as their entry for the contest, with a complicated voting system that basically boils down to songs being voted on by the viewing public. The winning country of each year’s competition generally gets to host the next year’s _Eurovision_, a rule that has led to a lot of controversy, especially as Israel has hosted the competition three times. In the U.K., television personality Rylan Clark, who got his start on _The X Factor,_ is co-presenter for the semi-final performance, while renowned Irish comedian and talk-show host, Graham Norton, hosts the finals.

Ncuti Gatwa himself, who plays the 15th Doctor, was scheduled to be the British spokesperson for this year’s _Eurovision Song Contest_, but pulled out due to “unforeseen circumstances.” Due to the timing of his cancellation, many took him pulling out as a protest of Israel’s qualification for the contest, which would be in keeping with Gatwa’s public stance on the conflict in Gaza. But there have been some who say that the episode “The Interstellar Song Contest” in itself had subtle nods to support of Palestine, not only in the episode’s themes of colonization and genocide, but also in the visual themes of the episode including the river at the center of the set design and the subtle use of watermelon imagery, which is associated with support for Palestine. Honestly, I wouldn’t put it past _Doctor Who_ to express their support publicly like that.

**And it’s at this point where I’m going to drop this week’s spoiler warning, so don’t read past here if you don’t want the episode spoiled for you.**

[![Image 2: CCC LB 2025](https://cdn.broadstreetads.com/assets/7a297666-601b-4dc1-b1b3-6eff11d6ab93.jpg)](https://denverconvention.com/ "CCC LB 2025")

![Image 3: Doctor Who](https://outfrontmagazineimages.s3.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/17183648/jpp_who_130324-02176_e1395d0c.jpeg)

_Photo courtesy of James Pardon/BBC Studios/Disney/Bad Wolf_

[PIN IT](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/bookmarklet/?url=https%3A%2F%2Foutfrontmagazine.com%2Ftv-review-the-doctor-who-episode-the-interstellar-song-contest-serves-up-major-surprises-and-a-pop-culture-tribute%2F&media=https%3A%2F%2Foutfrontmagazineimages.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2025%2F05%2F17183648%2Fjpp_who_130324-02176_e1395d0c.jpeg&description=Photo%20courtesy%20of%20James%20Pardon%2FBBC%20Studios%2FDisney%2FBad%20Wolf&is_video=false)
In the episode, The Fifteenth Doctor (Ncuti Gatwa) and Belinda (Varada Sethu), still trying to find a way to get Belinda home, land in the stadium that’s holding _The Interstellar Song Contest_, an extension of _Eurovision_ that has spread to the stars and now encompasses planets from across the Universe, held in a floating space stadium called The Harmony Auditorium and hosted by a cryogenically-suspended Rylan Clark (played by himself). When a terrorist named Kid (Freddie Fox), and his accomplice Wynn (Iona Anderson), of the horned species the Hellions, launch a terrorist attack on the event, almost all the spectators, including the Doctor, are sucked out of the stadium into a gravity shell where they slowly start freezing to death.

![Image 4: Doctor Who](https://outfrontmagazineimages.s3.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/17183658/jpp_who_250324-05130_bfea49cc.jpeg)

_Photo courtesy of James Pardon/BBC Studios/Disney/Bad Wolf_

[PIN IT](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/bookmarklet/?url=https%3A%2F%2Foutfrontmagazine.com%2Ftv-review-the-doctor-who-episode-the-interstellar-song-contest-serves-up-major-surprises-and-a-pop-culture-tribute%2F&media=https%3A%2F%2Foutfrontmagazineimages.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2025%2F05%2F17183658%2Fjpp_who_250324-05130_bfea49cc.jpeg&description=Photo%20courtesy%20of%20James%20Pardon%2FBBC%20Studios%2FDisney%2FBad%20Wolf&is_video=false)
The Doctor, barely conscious, is shocked awake by visions of his granddaughter Susan (Carole Ann Ford)—a character I’ve [written about before](https://outfrontmagazine.com/tv-review-doctor-who-episode-the-legend-of-ruby-sunday-teases-the-return-of-a-character-who-left-the-show-in-1964/) who has not been seen on the show since a cameo in the 20th anniversary special in 1983, and who hasn’t been a series regular since 1964. Susan urges the Doctor to keep fighting, and he finds a confetti cannon to shoot himself back to the stadium. There, he finds a lovely gay couple named Mike (Kadiff Kirwan) and Gary (Charlie Condou)—a nurse and a designer of the stadium, respectively—who help him regain control of the stadium from Kid and Wynn. The Doctor, thinking Belinda is dead, goes to a dark place and ends up torturing Kid as he outwits the terrorist.

![Image 5](https://outfrontmagazineimages.s3.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/17183707/sa903830_e4180e95.jpeg)

_Photo courtesy of Dan Fearon/BBC Studios/Disney/Bad Wolf_

[PIN IT](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/bookmarklet/?url=https%3A%2F%2Foutfrontmagazine.com%2Ftv-review-the-doctor-who-episode-the-interstellar-song-contest-serves-up-major-surprises-and-a-pop-culture-tribute%2F&media=https%3A%2F%2Foutfrontmagazineimages.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2025%2F05%2F17183707%2Fsa903830_e4180e95.jpeg&description=Photo%20courtesy%20of%20Dan%20Fearon%2FBBC%20Studios%2FDisney%2FBad%20Wolf&is_video=false)
Meanwhile, Belinda, who narrowly escaped being ejected from the stadium, meets another Hellion named Cora (Miriam-Teak Lee) who explains that a company called The Corporation destroyed their home planet to harvest poppies for artificial honey flavoring. Cora has cut her own horns off to fit in with the rest of society, a clear metaphor for the extremes that some people, including transgender people, have to go through to fit into society. With the attendees rescued, the contest is called off, but Cora gets the opportunity to sing a song in honor of the planet Hellia for their 3 trillion viewers.

As the Doctor and Belinda are leaving, they find a hologram based on Graham Norton (again, played by himself) who tells them of the history of Earth, which was destroyed on May 24, 2025. Having learned about the destruction of the planet on the very day that the Doctor is trying to get Belinda back to, he hurries back to that date with a promise to save the world once again.

But after the Doctor leaves, the mysterious Mrs. Flood (Anita Dobson)—whose secret identity has been a source of speculation since her first appearance in the 2023 Christmas special [“The Church on Ruby Road,”](https://outfrontmagazine.com/tv-review-doctor-who-christmas-special-the-church-on-ruby-road-is-fun-but-has-questionable-villains/) and who was an attendee at the contest—is revived, but admits that she’s already frozen her double brain stem, which is deadly to her as a Time Lady. With the Doctor gone, she attempts to regenerate, but instead bigenerates into two people (the second played by Archie Panjabi) and reveals herself to be The Rani, a classic series villain last seen in the 1987 serial “Time and the Rani.”

![Image 6: Doctor Who](https://outfrontmagazineimages.s3.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/17183726/jpp_who_110324-5_67bc1ae9.jpeg)

_Photo courtesy of James Pardon/BBC Studios/Disney/Bad Wolf_

[PIN IT](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/bookmarklet/?url=https%3A%2F%2Foutfrontmagazine.com%2Ftv-review-the-doctor-who-episode-the-interstellar-song-contest-serves-up-major-surprises-and-a-pop-culture-tribute%2F&media=https%3A%2F%2Foutfrontmagazineimages.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2025%2F05%2F17183726%2Fjpp_who_110324-5_67bc1ae9.jpeg&description=Photo%20courtesy%20of%20James%20Pardon%2FBBC%20Studios%2FDisney%2FBad%20Wolf&is_video=false)
Since The Rani hasn’t been seen in some time, it might be worthwhile to take a moment to introduce her. The Rani, originally played by the late Kate O’Mara, only appears in two classic episodes, both of which bear the character’s name in the title. In the sixth Doctor (Colin Baker) episode “The Mark of the Rani,” the Rani, an exiled Time Lady who has become the leader of a planet named Miasimia Goria. Always a scientist, but rarely an ethical one, the Rani conducts experiments on her followers which have left them unable to sleep, and therefore difficult to control. So the Rani sets herself up in various chaotic periods in Earth’s history, such as the American Revolution and the Luddite Riots, where it won’t be noticed that she’s stealing the chemical from humans that allows them to sleep, leaving her subjects restless and violent.

In her second appearance, the seventh Doctor (Sylvester McCoy) episode “Time and the Rani,” we find the Rani has now taken over the planet Lakertya and enslaved its people. She schemes to collect all of the minds of the greatest geniuses in the universe, such as Earth’s Albert Einstein, which she will collectively use to create a time manipulator, which will allow her to control any point in time that she wishes. Naturally, in both cases, The Doctor and his companions—Peri Brown (Nicola Bryant) in the first episode, Mel Bush (Bonnie Langford) in the second—foil the Rani’s plans on both occasions.

While the plots of classic series episodes may seem silly by today’s standards, there’s one take-away to remember about The Rani, and that’s that she’s not just a megalomaniacal maniac. She is that, but she’d never admit that power is her main motive. To her, she’s a scientist, and all of her plans are based in trying to carry out scientific experiments that just happen to put her in power as a final result. And she has very little interest in the ethical concerns of science, often leaving a trail of victims of her experimentation in her wake. So if her entire plan this time around is just about power and not about an experiment of some sort, I’ll be surprised.

But the Rani also frequently mocked The Master for his petty rivalry with the Doctor and thought seeking revenge against him was rather silly. Even in her second appearance, she seemed more interested in using the Doctor as part of her plan than she was in getting revenge against The Doctor. Considering that the newest incarnation of The Rani seems hellbent on revenge against the Doctor, I have to assume something has changed. In her last appearance in 1987, she was taken prisoner by the beings she had enslaved, much thanks to the Doctor, but it seems unlikely that they haven’t seen each other since then. Presumably, there’s another reason the Rani wants revenge.

In the end, the episode offered a one-two punch of surprise appearances from the classic series, all wrapped-up in one of the show’s most exciting pop-culture tributes. All-in-all, it makes for one of the best and most exciting episodes of the entire series, and one that I’m especially proud to say was written by a fellow trans woman writer. The coming two-part finale promises to be very exciting after this groundbreaking set-up, and I can’t wait to see what promises to be the explosive finale of the modern era of _Doctor Who_.

Rating: 96/100

### Written by Juno Dawson

"Welcome to the 803rd Interstellar Song Contest!"

**Episode Title****Premiere Date**
The Interstellar Song Contest 17/05/2025

The Doctor's quest to get Belinda back home to Earth leads to a space station hosting the famous song contest. But a harmless night of fun soon becomes a battle to survive.

* * *

### Plot

Seeking another Vindicator reading, in order to return to London on May 24th, 2025, [the Doctor](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/fifteenth-doctor) and [Belinda](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/belinda-chandra) land the [TARDIS](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/the-tardis) in the Harmony Arena, in the year 2925 – just in time for Rylan Clark to step out of cryogenesis to host the 803rd Interstellar Song Contest! As the 100,000-strong crowd erupts in applause, the Doctor and Belinda decide to stick around for the show.

As they settle in to watch the competition, trouble is brewing – [Mrs Flood](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/mrs-flood), sitting in the crowd, copies the Doctor’s Vindicator reading on her own device, stating it is “the final link” she needs. Meanwhile, in the gallery, the production team’s security Drone Guards are hijacked by an interloping [Hellion](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/hellions) known as ‘Kid’. The staff are escorted away, leaving Kid and his accomplice, another Hellion named Wynn, who had infiltrated the production team, in control of Harmony Arena and the show’s broadcast.

Switching the broadcast to the dress rehearsal, Kid then opens the air shield of Harmony Arena, flushing the audience into space. While Belinda escapes, the Doctor and the TARDIS are sucked into the vacuum of space! Kid and Wynn prepare to move onto the final phase of their plan – unleashing a Delta Wave through the broadcast, killing the three trillion viewers of the contest across the galaxy.

Frozen in space and barely conscious, the Doctor has a vision of his granddaughter, [Susan Foreman](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/susan-foreman), telling him to go back and find her. Waking up from his stasis, the Doctor uses a nearby confetti cannon to propel himself back to the Harmony Arena, where he is resuscitated by paramedic Mike, who was attending with his husband Gary.

As the Doctor, Mike and Gary look for answers, Belinda runs into more survivors in the Arena; including contest favourite Cora Saint Bavier, who was representing the planet Trion. When the survivors discover that Hellions are behind the attack, Cora reveals herself as a Hellion in hiding. She explains that Kid and Wynn are on a mission of vengeance against the event’s sponsor – who razed their native planet of Hellia for its natural resource, the Hell Poppy, and blamed the atrocity on the native population. Hellions are hated across the galaxy for this manufactured lie, and Kid plans to exact revenge on anyone he deems complicit - including all the viewers of the Interstellar Song Contest.

Enraged and vengeful, the Doctor seeks out the Hellions and destroys their Delta Wave device. He uses a hard-light hologram to repeatedly electrocute Kid – ignoring Susan’s pleas in his mind to stop – until he is reunited with Belinda. With the Hellions defeated, the Doctor, Belinda and their surviving allies work to rescue and revive the ejected audience members. After Harmony Arena is restored, Rylan introduces Cora Saint Bavier to the stage – who sings a song of Hellia, opening the hearts of the crowd to the plight of the Hellions.

As the Doctor and Belinda prepare to depart, they see a hologram of television presenter Graham Norton in the Arena’s museum wing – who informs them that Earth, for unknown reasons, “died” on May 24th, 2025. Setting off in the TARDIS to finally return to – and save – Belinda’s home, the pair look on in horror as the TARDIS doors explode open from the outside...

Meanwhile, one of the last concertgoers to be revived is none other than Mrs Flood, who – claiming her double brain stem has frozen – begins to regenerate! The resulting bi-generation reveals that all along, Mrs Flood has been the Doctor’s old nemesis, [the Rani](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/the-rani), in disguise. Taking the Vindicator readings, the two Ranis depart, ready to exact their final plan...

### Behind the Scenes

*   This episode sees the return of the Rani, portrayed by both Anita Dobson and Archie Panjabi. This is the first appearance of the Rani since the [Seventh Doctor](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/seventh-doctor)’s debut adventure [_Time and the Rani_](https://www.doctorwho.tv/stories/time-and-the-rani) in 1987.
*   Carole Ann Ford reprises her role as the Doctor’s granddaughter Susan Foreman for the first time in the TV series since [_The Five Doctors_](https://www.doctorwho.tv/stories/the-five-doctors) in 1983. She also reprised the role in 1993's _Dimensions in Time_.
*   _The Interstellar Song Contest_ was written by Juno Dawson, whose previous work in the Whoniverse includes [Thirteenth Doctor](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/thirteenth-doctor) novel _The Good Doctor_ and both seasons of the original audio drama _Doctor Who: Redacted_.
*   Singer Christine Rotondo, who plays contestant Liz Lizardine, has previously appeared in Doctor Who as the voice of ‘Janis Goblin’, the singer of the [Goblin](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/the-goblins) band in [_The Church on Ruby Road_](https://www.doctorwho.tv/stories/the-church-on-ruby-road).
*   TV host and Eurovision commentator Graham Norton makes an appearance as a hologram of himself. This marks Norton’s first official appearance in Doctor Who, although idents for _The Graham Norton Show_ have appeared onscreen during pivotal scenes in episodes aired on BBC One – a running joke amongst Doctor Who fans!
*   Cora's aria at the end of the episode was composed by Murray Gold, with lyrics translated by Juno Dawson. They are as follows:
From pastures gold to hills so blue

Bless'd suns bring life anew

Hellia, spectacular

A star to ever guide us home

From settlers first to babes a born

Lo exalted thy twin horns

Hellia, illustria

Kin from kin, sky to heart

Hellia! Hellia!

Dignity be thy name

Hellia! Hellia!

Bastion of the brave

Hellia! Hellia! Our home.

![Image 1: Doctor Who](https://www.doctorwhotv.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/interstellar-head-hurts.jpg)

_J.C. reviews the sixth episode of Series 15._

Before watching this week’s _Doctor Who_, I’d just finished the eighth episode of Season 2 of _Andor_ (I’m a bit behind and catching up), and my god, was that a bad idea. The contrast could not have been starker. _Andor_ was serious, considered science fiction, sharply written, and beautifully acted. Its characters faced impossible choices, and the show refused to offer easy answers or fall back on black-and-white morality. What the episode built, minute by minute, was dread, a slow, suffocating tension that crept up until it finally exploded. You didn’t just watch things unfold, you felt them closing in. The action, when it came, was grounded and brutal. It was confident, grown-up storytelling, and easily some of the most powerful television I’ve seen this year. In short, it was genre TV at the peak of its craft.

And then I watched _Doctor Who…_ I was immediately greeted by a space furry and a real-life Ken doll fresh out of cryogenic freeze, kicking off a campy song contest while silly aliens pranced about in the audience. Talk about whiplash!

“The Interstellar Song Contest” is initially set up as a Eurovision spoof in space, but it can’t seem to decide what it wants to be. One minute it’s a confetti-drenched musical extravaganza, the next it’s half-heartedly dealing with genocide, revenge, and political oppression. The simplistic plot feels stitched together from offcuts of better _Doctor Who_ stories. The Doctor and Belinda arrive just in time for a universe-wide song contest, which is promptly hijacked by a villain named Kid, who plans to murder the audience using a psychic brainwave transmitted through the broadcast.

I was baffled to learn this was the most expensive episode of _Doctor Who_ ever made. For me, it only fleetingly looked the part. Then again, I had just watched _Andor_, which wears its nearly $300 million budget a season in every frame. Perhaps _Doctor Who_‘s set cheapness was intentional, meant to match the Eurovision’s trashy aesthetic, but it ends up undermining the drama. That said…

![Image 2](https://www.doctorwhotv.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/interstellar-space-attack.jpg)

This almost silent shot of the audience being blasted into space, was a rare moment where Doctor Who embraces visual poetry and dark horror. If only the rest of the episode followed through and matched this level of maturity and narrative weight.

There is, however, one legitimately stunning sequence early on when the arena’s air shield collapses, blasting the audience and the Doctor into space. Kudos to the CGI artists. It was genuinely haunting as bodies slowly float away and freeze, leaving us to reflect on the apparent atrocity. For a moment, it feels like current _Doctor Who_ might actually commit to some real stakes. But sadly, as is so often the case, the show soon walks it back. Turns out the “mavity” field has suspended them in a state of preservation (I’m so over mavity). The Doctor himself inexplicably survives thanks to a random vision of Susan (more on her later) somehow restoring him, and then launches himself back with a confetti cannon, also somehow managing to shout while he’s riding it in space. Sigh. And so what seemed like a mass genocidal attack becomes a large-scale rescue op instead.

Ncuti Gatwa feels adrift in this episode, where he’s required to juggle his usual campy, energetic self with something far darker later on. He gets his own attempt at more of a [Time Lord Victorious](https://www.doctorwhotv.co.uk/5-of-tennants-best-doctor-who-episode-performances-93823.htm) moment when he catches up to and repeatedly tortures Kid. The scene felt unearned, arriving abruptly with little build-up. It took a lot of groundwork for David Tennant’s Doctor to reach that kind of darkness. Here, it happens in minutes. And while I appreciate a darker character turn when it’s done well, the Doctor outright repeatedly torturing someone doesn’t sit right with me. There’s a big difference between darkness and cruelty. Remember, “Never cruel or cowardly”? RTD doesn’t seem to. It’s also resolved far too quickly, with the Doctor and Belinda heading off without ever really addressing it.

Speaking of. Belinda’s given a few tender scenes and plays a key role in grounding the Doctor again, though it could have been handled better. There’s no real character growth. After spending most of the previous two episodes off-screen and spending much of this one either panicked or sidelined, she suddenly turns to the Doctor and calls him “wonderful”. This comes not long after witnessing him torture someone, which makes the emotional payoff feel hollow. Their relationship has barely been developed across this season. Her praise feels less like a genuine character moment and more like a scripted beat the show hasn’t earned.

![Image 3](https://www.doctorwhotv.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/Doctor-Who-Interstellar-Promo-Pics-3.jpg)

Then there’s Kid, our main villain of the week. He’s the latest in a long line of angry young men (I’m seeing a pattern here), and while his backstory has more weight than Alan or Conrad’s, it’s still too little, too late. We learn that his planet, the inventively named Hellia, was destroyed by corporate greed, harvested, stripped, and left barren for the sake of honey flavouring. That’s a disturbing concept, and his desire for revenge could have made him a more sympathetic figure. But instead of exploring that with nuance, the show plays it big and broad. His plan to hijack the broadcast and kill three trillion viewers with a psychic brainwave is cartoonishly over the top, and the script never gives him the depth or internal conflict needed to make it land. The show gestures at systemic critique, but ends up falling back on familiar clichés, the damaged outcast with a grudge, lashing out at the galaxy. With more time and stronger writing, Kid could have been an interesting antagonist.

Surrounding the Doctor is a rotating cast of guest stars. Rylan Clark plays a heightened version of himself, not much of a stretch, but Graham Norton rather surprisingly delivers as a hologram version. Miriam-Teak Lee as Cora is also decent. Her final performance, a ballad from her lost homeworld, isn’t bad and almost justifies her arc. But even that is nearly drowned out by the constant tonal zig-zagging. The show never lets any emotion settle any more. The gay couple, Mike and Gary, seem to be there to mostly resolve plot points all too conveniently. They just happen to have the exact skills needed to save the day, one’s a nurse, the other a hologram technician with expert knowledge of triangulation. The Doctor himself jokes about how convenient it all is, but pointing out the issue doesn’t make it go away.

![Image 4](https://www.doctorwhotv.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/Doctor-Who-Wish-World-Promo-Pics-10.jpg)

Just when it seems like the story has wrapped up, we get one last twist, the Rani is back. Or rather, two Ranis. I doubt this reveal landed as big as RTD hoped, with rumours swirling for months. And it’s another bi-generation already. So much for this “mythical” event. The reveal itself lacks tension or mystique (and with a rather cheap-looking effect too). It’s thrown in as if trying to mimic a Marvel-style mid-credits teaser, instead of building toward it [_masterfully_](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FI_RB2URZPY) in the episode like with past major villain reveals. Also, Anita Dobson’s character hasn’t acted remotely like the Rani up to this point. It feels like RTD retrofitting the name onto Mrs Flood rather than planning it from the start. And Flood-Rani’s suddenly all subservient? Why?

There’s also a bigger question: is the Rani’s return even necessary at this point? Missy already explored the idea of a female Time Lord antagonist in a layered, memorable way. This Rani seems like she’ll continue to be a pantomime villain (admittedly, it’s early days, so I can only hope there’s more to it). Also, now that gender fluidity is standard for Time Lords, the idea of a “Time Lady” villain doesn’t feel especially relevant now. If anything, it raises a fair question, would they ever make the Rani a man now? Or does it only work one way?

Finally, there’s Susan. Her brief appearance as some sort of vision is undeniably pleasing, a callback many fans have waited decades to see. But it’s little more than a cameo. After being teased throughout Series 14, her return finally happens here, randomly, and with no real narrative weight. If RTD was able to get Carole Ann Ford back all along, why not use her in the 60th anniversary specials, where it would have made far more historical sense? Instead, her reappearance is cryptic, fleeting, and sadly underwhelming (for now).

“The Interstellar Song Contest” wants to be a lot of things, a love letter to Eurovision, a satire of corporate greed, a tragic fable of lost worlds, but in trying to be all of them at once, it ends up being none of them. It’s loud, messy, and emotionally scattered. What should be a symphony of genres ends up as little more than noise.

Doctor Who season 2 is in full flow, with the second episode – which our [review](https://www.gamesradar.com/entertainment/sci-fi-shows/doctor-who-season-2-episode-2-lux/) called "bold, bonkers" – having dropped last Saturday. The partially animated 'Lux' isn't the only unusual installment this season, however. The upcoming sixth episode, 'The Interstellar Song Contest' is set to mix the worlds of Doctor Who with another iconic institution: Eurovision!

Speaking exclusively in the new issue of [SFX magazine](https://www.cinemablend.com/uk/sfx), which features The Walking Dead: Dead City season 2 on the cover, the episode's writer, Juno Dawson, explained how she came to pen it.

The idea for the episode originated with Doctor Who showrunner Russell T. Davies, Dawson explained to SFX: "Russell is a workhorse who doesn't seem to need sleep, he emailed me at about 1:30 in the morning," the writer revealed.

"I didn't see it until my alarm went off at 7am," Dawson continued. "Like any modern person, the first \[thing\] I did was check my phone – like an addict. And I had this email saying, 'Die Hard meets Eurovision. What do you think?'

"I handed the phone to my then-husband, and I was like, 'Am I imagining this?' He was just like, 'Oh my god'. Like, the call had finally come! It was the easiest 'yes' I've ever said."

Dawson also said that she had initially initially pitched an episode inspired by classic disaster movie, The Poseidon Adventure, but it would have been prohibitively expensive to make.

"I look back now with a slight cringe," she added of that idea. "What was I thinking? It was very ambitious. The bare bones are still in the finished product but, God, in one version I had robots wearing lederhosen! They've gone!"

**Storyline**

Welcome to the 803rd Interstellar Song Contest in the year 2925. The Doctor and Belinda are delighted when the Tardis lands in the Harmony Arena space station but, as the entertainment commences, the show is sabotaged and the audience are expelled into space. The hijackers are led by Kid, a vengeful Hellion, whose home world Hellia was pillaged for poppy honey by the corporation promoting the contest. He plans to transmit a delta wave to wipe out the three trillion viewers. The Doctor intercedes with considerable rage, but is having strange visions of his granddaughter Susan. Mrs Flood is revealed to be the Doctor’s Time Lord adversary the Rani. She bi-generates and both incarnations follow the Doctor and Belinda back to Earth...

**RT review by Patrick Mulkern**

I can’t stick Rylan, not for love or money. An instant turn-off on air. But he’s actually very good in Doctor Who and it made me like him. That’s how strong and persuasive this episode is. Graham Norton I love, and his hologram form here is a lovely answer to the two occasions when he popped up unwanted (thanks to BBC Presentation) in earlier programmes. Now he’s a harbinger of the cataclysm that befalls Earth in 2025. So far, so Eurovision with these two. I was half expecting the ghosts of Terry Wogan and Katie Boyle to manifest.

This futuristic, interstellar spin on Eurovision is simply magnificent. From the epic stadium lightshow to the hordes of squealing fans, to snatches of quirky songs in the final to the soaring anthem that Cora sings. Even if the intercut reactions to the gawping cast edge it towards mawkish, Miriam-Teak Lee belts her song out of the arena. Winner of the 2020 Olivier Award for Best Actress in a Musical for & Juliet, she’s great casting here; and perhaps the new songwriting partnership of Russell T Davies, Juno Dawson and Murray Gold should be representing Royaume Uni. The burst of Bucks Fizz’s 1981 winning entry Making Your Mind Up, when the expelled crowds are being saved, is a total hoot.

This is a return to peak RTD, channelled through Dawson, who gets sole writing credit. The joy of this episode is that it is, rightly, as camp as… well, Eurovision… but it is also a gripping adventure, simple to follow, with winning and believable characters. Freddie Fox is superb as the fanatical villain “Kid”, a horned beast from the planet Hellia. His motivation and vengeful nature are also clear. Kadiff Kirwan and Charlie Condou are lovely as Mike and Gary, the couple who stop bickering to make a valuable contribution and go weak at the knees in the presence of the Time Lord.

Best of all, Ncuti Gatwa really is the Doctor here, fully formed and multi-faceted. Mercurial, in that he’s warm and fun-loving on arrival at the Harmony Arena, but also ice-cold when blasting painful retribution into the squirming Kid. He also dazzles everyone he meets with total conviction. Star quality. This is Gatwa’s finest episode yet.

And then we come to Susan. Beautifully filmed, dream-like glimpses of Carole Ann Ford, one of the original stars of Doctor Who in 1963 and 64, now in her 80s. After all the red herrings last year with Susan Twist, how magical to have Susan back in Doctor Who, entering the Doctor’s mind and calling him “Grandfather”. I’ve grown tired of the sausage factory of mystery women in recent times, but Susan is the original enigma at the birth of Doctor Who. The stuff of legends.

10.title: Doctor Who Trailer Breakdown
10.description: The latest Doctor Who trailers give us our first real idea of the universe of adventures and terrors which await us on the 12th of April
10.content:
[![Image 1: A new adventure begins when a weird spatial anomaly passes through the TARDIS , BBC Studios/Bad Wolf,James Pardon. The Doctor holds on to a level on the console with one hand, his other outstretched](https://www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/504680-scaled.jpg)](https://i0.wp.com/www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/504680-scaled.jpg?fit=2560%2C1707&quality=89&ssl=1)

A new adventure begins when a weird spatial anomaly passes through the TARDIS , BBC Studios/Bad Wolf,James Pardon

The latest Doctor Who trailers make clear that we’re in for a universe of adventure!
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The recent Doctor Who trailer gave us our best look yet at the upcoming season. But before we jump aboard the TARDIS with the Doctor and Belinda next month, we can take a deeper dive into what we know about their adventures. Blogtor Who must give you fair warning, though. This article may just be speculation based on officially released BBC publicity. However, you may want to go into the new season completely cold. If so, you should consider everything from this point on spoilers.

[![Image 2: The TARDIS encounters a weird spatial anomaly. The Doctor looks around the console room, curious](https://i0.wp.com/www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/DW-2-1-1-Doctor-Notices.png?resize=3840%2C1690&quality=80)](https://i0.wp.com/www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/DW-2-1-1-Doctor-Notices.png?quality=80)

The TARDIS encounters a weird spatial anomaly

[![Image 3: The Doctor pulls a lever on the TARDIS console](https://i0.wp.com/www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/DW-2-1-1A-Pull-the-Lever.png?resize=3840%2C1680&quality=80)](https://i0.wp.com/www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/DW-2-1-1A-Pull-the-Lever.png?quality=80)

The Doctor pulls a lever on the TARDIS console

[![Image 4: The TARDIS flies towards the Earth](https://i0.wp.com/www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/DW-2-1-1AA-TARDIS-heading-for-Earth.png?resize=3840%2C1674&quality=80)](https://i0.wp.com/www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/DW-2-1-1AA-TARDIS-heading-for-Earth.png?quality=80)

The TARDIS flies towards the Earth

[![Image 5: The Doctor pokes his head out of the TARDIS door](https://i0.wp.com/www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/DW-2-1-1AAA-Doctor-Checking-It-Out.png?resize=3840%2C1686&quality=80)](https://i0.wp.com/www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/DW-2-1-1AAA-Doctor-Checking-It-Out.png?quality=80)

The Doctor pokes his head out of the TARDIS door

[![Image 6: Belinda is woken by strange lights outside her window](https://i0.wp.com/www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/DW-2-1-1AAAA-Belinda-Bed.png?resize=3840%2C1678&quality=80)](https://i0.wp.com/www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/DW-2-1-1AAAA-Belinda-Bed.png?quality=80)

Belinda is woken by strange lights outside her window

[![Image 7: Belinda, seen from behind, looks through her bedroom window at a descending rocket ship](https://i0.wp.com/www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/DW-2-1-2-Belinda-Window-1.png?resize=3840%2C1678&quality=80)](https://i0.wp.com/www.blogtorwho.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/DW-2-1-2-Belinda-Window-1.png?quality=80)

Belinda looks through her bedroom window at a descending rocket ship

### Episode 1: Doctor Who’s Homage to Flash Gordon

We don’t have titles for any of the episodes yet. Indeed, even though we know the writing team for this season, we don’t have exact details of who has written what. Plus, we only have a general idea of the running order for these stories. But we do know that episode one features Ncuti Gatwa’s Doctor meeting his latest new friend, Belinda Chandra (Varada Sethu.)
